statements.text: An aria-describedby on the host is resolved against ids in the host's own root and applied to the inner input together with the supporting text, in browsers with ARIA element reflection.

examples.html: <violet-text-field disabled label="Plant name" name="plantName" placeholder="Unavailable while sync is running" supporting-text="Disabled fields should stay visibly unavailable without losing structure." type="search"></violet-text-field>
<violet-text-field invalid label="Quantity" name="quantity" placeholder="Enter quantity" required supporting-text="Required before checkout can continue." type="text"></violet-text-field>

<violet-text-field label="Plant name" name="plantName" placeholder="Search cultivated rows" required supporting-text="Use this for quick filtering or manual entry." type="search"><violet-icon decorative icon="system/search" label slot="before"></violet-icon></violet-text-field>

summary: Single-line text input with a built-in label and supporting text, for text, search, email, url, password, tel, number or date entry.

usage.text: The required, type, pattern, min, max, step, minlength and maxlength attributes feed validity. Whitespace-only text counts as missing when required. A readonly field is never reported invalid, even with invalid set.
The change event fires when the native input commits: on blur after an edit, or on Enter.
There is no error-text attribute and no error message is rendered: invalid only turns the border red and sets aria-invalid. Put the error wording in supporting-text while invalid.
The before slot holds leading inline content such as a search icon; mark an icon there decorative so it is not read.
